history.period: Ancient legend (unverifiable; says installed by Rama 3000 BCE); moved to present site 1566; 450 years completed May 2011; major reconstruction 1905; sabha mandap added 1951
history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 223 (Shree Ramnath Temple) and seq 243 (Shri Ramnath Temple) — the same Ramnathim temple, written again per-row. CSV town is WRONG: the temple is at Ramnathim, Bandivade (Bandora), Ponda taluka, North Goa — not Vasco da Gama. The original temple stood at Loutolim in Salcete (South Goa); in 1566 the villagers migrated with their deities to Bandora in the Antruz Mahal region (then under the Bijapur Sultanate) to escape Portuguese temple destruction, and built five temples for the five deities — this is the panchayatan of Ramnath (chief deity, 'Lord of Rama', i.e. Shiva), Shanteri/Shantadurga (from Rivona), Kamakshi (from Loutolim), Lakshmi Narayan, Siddhinath (Ganesh), plus Betal and Kalbhairav. The temple is a kuldev of Goud Saraswat Brahmins (Vatsa and Kaundinya gotras), Daivadnya Brahmins and Vaishyas.

name: Shri Ramnath Temple (Ramnathi)
town_description: Ramnathim is a temple village at Bandivade (Bandora) in Ponda taluka, North Goa, about 22 km from Panaji. It lies in the Antruz Mahal area where many Goan Hindu shrines were relocated during the 16th-century Portuguese temple-destruction campaign, and it is today a quiet pilgrimage centre and kuldev seat for Goud Saraswat Brahmin families spread along the western coast of India.
